original_card.question: Can a new local cost interface change the deficit-to-recursive-cost ratio beyond current packing?
methods: Propose a changed helper inventory and derive an optimistic exact moment.
Design a small completed instance and independently verify its endpoint and rank bill.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A new physically realizable contract outside the frozen catalogue whose per-call profile, screened with ceiling.ceiling(), beats the selected word's packing ceiling; a lower cap does not establish identical circuitry or order attainable optima, and is insufficient to pass the stronger-budget target under this model. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Packing of the selected word is capped at +0.87% (ceiling model); only a lower local excess spend or a changed coverage law raises the cap.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one changed boundary or helper type with explicit counts.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Mixing only providers already inside the pinned catalogue.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: Price a bit-free version of the selected complex local word: every address map (or skew kernel) is implemented by complex-side operations only, never by the bit supplier's chunk swaps; find which cost terms dominate and whether any layout schedule, compiler or skew-kernel tape procedure can keep the saving positive.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a new local cost interface that beats the packing ceiling. This package instead asks whether the complex supplier can drop its dependence on the bit supplier at all (the open self-contained-supplier route of research/kappa01-outer-repair), which would make kappa depend on the complex side alone. It changes the cost interface (address maps become recursive children or skew kernels) but answers a feasibility question, not a ceiling-beating one.
bottleneck_link: kappa = min(complex, bit). research/kappa01-outer-repair shows the bit side could be built from complex calls by Walsh identities, but only if the complex supplier itself is bit-free. Section 05 uses the bit supplier only for chunk swaps inside packed row additions (basis changes P_M per edge). This package prices replacing them and finds every variant negative, so that route cannot remove the bit cap for this word/family.
stop_rule: Stop when every variant has an exact price and the remaining escape routes are reduced to a stated lower bound or to the bit supplier itself.
evidence: verify.py (about 40 s, standard library) replays: control reproduction of the ADAPTER-FUSION relative compiler (232198 / 239648 rank mass); a lazy-direction compiler halving it (114114 / 127308; saving about -0.90 / -0.93); children alone force 0 / 8 layout changes; ADD gates force at least 105 / 106 layout changes per call under any schedule versus a budget of about 35 rank units (17 changes); greedy shared-layout schedule 2921 / 3177; skew kernels with minimum-weight residual bases: mean direction weight 2.73, saving -0.26 (per-bit flips) to -0.155 (256-tape multiway split, one level only); pass-model lemmas (LDS of XOR permutations = 2^W, submultiplicativity, prefix-reversal basis, bit-reordering invariance, controlled block reversal = shear).
author: Mark (Matarener)
ai_assistance: Investigation, code and text prepared with Claude (Anthropic) assistance on the donor's computer; the donor directed the questions. No independent human review.

open_questions.question: Is there a complex network outside the subspace-label family (sections 03/05) whose saving does not require many non-orthogonal lines meeting at one gate?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Every bit-free variant here fails because the source of the rank saving (many lines in a low-dimensional label space) is exactly what forces layout changes or growing skew masks.
open_questions.first_step: State the per-data-wire margin (below 1 rank unit) versus the minimum cost of one layout change (2 rank units) for a candidate network before building it.
open_questions.blocked_by: No such network family is known in the repository.

open_questions.question: Exact minimum number of layout changes for the selected word (now between 105 and about 3000 per call).
open_questions.why_it_matters: Refines the gap; it cannot make the word profitable because the lower bound already exceeds the budget about six times.
open_questions.first_step: Formulate the shared-layout schedule as a set-cover / ILP over gate windows and solve it with CP-SAT.

open_questions.question: A multitape lower bound for XOR-by-mask permutations outside the pass model.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would close the skew-kernel route unconditionally.
open_questions.first_step: Note that XOR-by-mask reduces to transposition plus one reversal, so the bit supplier already beats W passes; an unconditional bound would bound transposition and, through section 10, multiplication.
open_questions.blocked_by: Superlinear multitape lower bounds of this kind are a well-known open problem.
